html:
Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan was a Pakistani singer of qawwali, the devotional music of the Sufis, born in 1948 in Lyallpur, now Faisalabad, a city of the Punjab canal colonies.

He came from a family of qawwals going back centuries and led its party from 1971. His huge voice, his long improvised runs and his stamina, often singing for hours, made him a star across South Asia. He recorded well over a hundred albums.

In the 1980s and 1990s he worked with Western musicians such as Peter Gabriel and on film soundtracks, and his fusion records brought qawwali to listeners who had never heard of Sufism. He died in London in 1997, aged 48. His songs are still covered constantly, on Coke Studio and in Bollywood films.
